section_b_architectural_compatibility_as.cp_2_5_d2_iii_conflict_origin: Recorded at CP 2.5 close ([[cipher-cp25-closed]]): may13 design conflicted with cipher_rt_phase4's GOT patcher. Concrete nature of conflict needed verification (read-only audit).
what_we_found: cipher_rt_phase4 today imports 18+ may13 source files (oracle, recipes, kernel_table, runtime, telemetry, etc.) — see Makefile lines 78-84. The OBSERVER/ACTUATOR layer ports cleanly.
cipher_rt_phase4 has NOT imported cipher_intercept.cpp, cipher_intercept_cudart.cpp, or cipher_graph_inspect.cpp — the driver-API interception layer.

cipher_rt_phase4's current driver-side touch points are: (1) cipher_cupti.c CUPTI callback line 162 (passive observation), (2) cuBLAS GOT patcher targeting cublasGemmEx + cublasLtMatmul + 17 LT variants, (3) ATen SDPA trampolines for attention. NONE of these overlap the driver-API entry points may13's cipher_intercept_cudart.cpp hooks (which target the LAUNCH path itself + module-load + cuGetProcAddress, not cuBLAS).

Therefore the historical 'conflict' is bounded to: (a) init-order issues — may13 uses constructor(101) + cipher_rt_phase4 auto-init has its own priority chain; (b) overlapping CUPTI vs LD_PRELOAD launch observation; (c) potential double-counting of cuBLAS calls if both layers GOT-patch cuBLAS (may13 + phase4 each have separate cuBLAS hooks).
section_b_architectural_compatibility_as.structural_compatibility_verdict: NON-CONFLICTING in code at driver-API + module-load + graph layers — these are gaps in cipher_rt_phase4 today, not overlaps. The cuBLAS layer in may13 IS a duplicate of cipher_rt_phase4's existing hook and would need explicit reconciliation (drop may13's cuBLAS shim during port, keep phase4's CUDA-13 + Path B' assembly trampolines instead).
section_b_architectural_compatibility_as.phase_a_finding_recall: [[v1-phase-a-driver-worker-init]]: modern CUDA uses cuGetProcAddress lazy resolution which bypasses LD_PRELOAD constructor + dlsym hook. Phase A picked CUDA_INJECTION64_PATH (driver-mediated active invocation). may13's mechanism is cuGetProcAddress redirection — that IS what Phase A also does inside the InitializeInjection2 callback. So may13's interception mechanism is portable; only the .so constructor wrapper around it needs adjustment to fire via InitializeInjection2 instead of constructor().
